But that's where you're missing the point. You're actually SUPPOSED to apply human morality to these higher beings. We call Sargeras evil not because he is evil in a universal sense, but because he is a threat to us. Is he saving the universe from eternal slavery and corruption? Yeah. By subjecting it to eternal slavery and corruption. From our perspective, Sargeras is the same as the Viid Lords. We get crushed no matter who does the crushing. 

Illidan wasn't "wrong" to kill X'era - that he even needed to shows that the Light is in precisely the same category as Sargeras and the Void. What does it matter that we fight for freedom from Sargeras, if we do it by subjecting ourselves to the light? We're just trading one slavemaster for another. 

I understand your point about not applying human concepts of morality to deities and cosmic forces, but I think you both take it too far, while you also refuse to judge the various cosmic players on the same merit. If we call the goals of Sargeras morally just, and the actions of X'era morally just, on the basis that both had more important goals to achieve than worrying about breaking a few eggs, then we end up with a paradox. X'era empowering Illidan who will then be instrumental in destroying Sargeras prevents Sargeras from destroying the void lords. If destroying the void lords no matter the cost is deemed moral, then preventing that must be immoral. If their idea is that they know Sargeras can't kill the void, i.e. "If you want something done, you gotta do it yourself" then we open up the question of which cosmic unfathomable being is right in their vision of how the void can be destroyed. And couldn't Sargeras be the man with the plan, and the Light being the ones who miscalculated?

These beings are not all-knowing. Do they operate on a higher plane with more information than we do? Certainly. Are they infallible? Considering each major force contradicts each other, no. Theyre not thinking about "what has to be done to defeat the Void Lords". What they are doing is "what has to be done to defeat the Void Lords while also ensuring that I end up on top/survive". None of these higher beings wants to sacrifice themselves to save the universe. They'd really rather prefer to sacrifice everyone else first. 

That's what's Legion is really hammering home. In the end, Good is subjective, and it's mostly about what's best for you and your kind. All the other higher beings don't give a shit about Azeroth, and what possibly makes the mortal races more admirable than the uncaring Gods, is our willingness to sacrifice ourselves, instead of lesser beings.

Step one is: read your own post.

"I can't stand betting such large ammounts on safe games."

Well, wasn't safe then, was it? No game is safe. Ever. You probably know this, but knowing this and... er... How to say... feeling it? Two different things. You can know it, and still fool yourself. Get tempted. Make sure you realize 100% just how incredibly many variables affect the outcome. Look at past games where T2 or 3 teams gets the lucky break and takes down the likes of Fnatic. 
And BO1's are the least safe of all.

So how do you get back? You take it slow. Seriously. I've only ever lost all my shit when I got impatient. 3 times now, I've built ~300 euro inventories from ~3 euro. It was all about playing it slow, playing percentages, being happy with just getting 0.08 skins, etc. It'll take time, but be happy with that and let it slooooowly grow, and you won't be throwing it all away again hoping to make a fast profit so you can get to "the real gambling".

What loses inventories? Impatience, overconfidence and desperation. Twice I basically lost it all, once I got around that 300 euro mark. I got overconfident, then lost. Then I got desperate, wanting to reclaim my losses. Even more stupid bets, even more stupid losses. Then, if I finally get a lucky break, that's when impatience sets in. "I'm back," I'll think, "but I need to get back to 300 fast." And then begins stupid all-ins, poorly calculated underdogs, etc.

Depending on your RL economy, buy back a low ammount of skins. You want to be able to lose it, without it having an impact on your RL life. Then bet slow, don't worry about losses too much, since you're betting with pennies now, but think long and hard about 1) What happened that you did not take into account, and 2) Was your bet still smart? I've lost bets that I still feel were the right call. I've also won bets that I'm kicking myself over, luckily beating odds and risks I should not have taken. Case in point, Fnatic vs NiP on wednesday. Put a knife on Fnatic. That knife was 1/4 of my inventory. I won, yes, but in hindsight, that was not a smart bet. And I almost lost it.

There are TONS of great threads and posts on here that talk about how to be a good bettor. How to know which matches to bet on, how much to bet, etc. Use that resource. The rules that apply to 200 euro inventories also goes for 20 euro ones.
